描述_ZN: The booklet "Visiting the Stele at Dai Lu", Qing Dynasty, painted by Huang Yi, on paper, color, 17.4 cm per opening, 50.8 cm across.　　The name of the picture "Dai" refers to Mount Tai, located in the central part of Shandong Province. The book "visiting the monuments in Dai Lu" has 24 openings, depicting Huang Yi in the second year of the Qing Dynasty (1797) from Jining to visit the monuments in Mount Tai in the form of left text and right picture. According to the author's own inscription, some of the pages record the inscriptions on Mount Tai, such as "Daeding", "Kaiyuan Mill Cliff Tablet", "Shijing Valley", "Wangmu Pond", etc, "The other part records the inscriptions the author saw on his way to and from the site, such as "Daming Lake", "Mencius Temple", "Confucius Forest ", "Confucius Temple", "Dawenkou" and so on. In addition, the author also introduces the specific condition of the inscriptions in his inscriptions, providing information for future generations to study.　　Huang Yi devoted his life to the study of jinshi steles and tablets, and has searched around for the surviving broken steles and organized and recorded them in a more systematic way, which has played an active role in the development of traditional jinshiology in China. Unusually, he personally used a brush to record the process of each visit to ancient monuments in full, and drew many works, which were widely praised by artists of the time. One of these works is the booklet "Visiting Monuments in Dailu".　　Throughout the whole set, the author uses two Chinese painting techniques, ink and light violet, but presents a unified artistic style. Specifically, he pays attention to the interruptions and transitions of the lines, and mostly uses thick strokes and short lines to depict the scenery around the location of the inscriptions, making the scene simple and clear, with a secluded and quiet mood, and a bland and naive artistic interest.
